question: The Rohtasgarh or Rohtas Fort is located in which river valley?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Son**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rohtasgarh or Rohtas Fort is located in the Son River valley.
 
• It is situated in the Rohtas district of the Indian state of Bihar.
 
• The fort is a renowned historical and cultural site, perched atop the Kaimur Hills.
 
• Rohtasgarh Fort is one of the largest and strongest hill forts in India, famous for its architectural grandeur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Son River:**

 
 
• The Son River is the second-largest southern tributary of the Ganges after the Yamuna.
 
• It originates near Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows north-northwest through Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Bihar before joining the Ganges near Patna.
 
• The river is known for its seasonal flow and carries a significant amount of silt and sand.
 
• The Son River valley is rich in history and has several archaeological sites, including the Rohtasgarh Fort.
 
 
 
• **Rohtasgarh Fort:**
 
 
• The fort is believed to have been built by Raja Harishchandra of the Solar dynasty.
 
• It was named after his son, Rohitashva, and has been a strategic military site for various empires, including the Mughals and the British.
 
• The fort complex includes numerous structures, such as palaces, temples, mosques, and waterfalls.
 
• Rohtasgarh Fort is a popular tourist destination and holds great archaeological and historical significance.
 
 
 
• **Kaimur Hills:**
 
 
• The Kaimur Range is the eastern portion of the Vindhya Range, extending from Madhya Pradesh through Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Jharkhand.
 
• The hills are known for their rich biodiversity, including various flora and fauna.
 
• The Kaimur Hills are also home to several ancient rock paintings and caves.
 
• The region is a significant part of the cultural and natural heritage of India.
